title: Adaptive Prefetch & Route-Fallback Governor for Safe Cost Auto-Tuning
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an adaptive controller that recommends and safely applies batching and KV-prefetch profiles while enforcing latency and throughput SLOs through routing limiters and automated fallback. The controller must run experiments (shadow + gradual canary), detect anomalous regressions using streaming change-point detectors, and automatically rollback or fanout traffic to conservative routes when risk thresholds are hit.
acceptance_criteria: Controller produces per-workload batching and prefetch recommendations with expected cost delta and latency impact estimates
Staged apply flow: shadow -> 1% canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic pause/rollback on SLO breach
Anomaly detector flags p95/p99 latency regressions and throughput drops within 5 minutes of onset
Route-fallback policy exists to divert affected traffic to pinned low-latency variants or smaller batch profiles without manual intervention
End-to-end test (integration) demonstrates safe rollback triggered by synthetic tail-latency spike
Docs and runbook published with clear owner and SLI thresholds
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototype recommendation model that ingests request size distribution, token histograms, and KV-hit rates; output candidate batch sizes and prefetch window
Phase 2: Build canary pipeline with traffic shaping and shadow apply capability; add tagging to traces for config-version
Phase 3: Integrate streaming anomaly detector (EWMA + ADWIN change-point) and define SLO gates for auto-pause/rollback
Phase 4: Implement route-fallback policies and a lightweight circuit limiter that reduces batch_size or routes to variant when p99>threshold
Phase 5: Run controlled experiments on non-critical tenant pool, validate economics, iterate thresholds
Phase 6: Bake into Optimize advisor with opt-in toggle and console controls
rollback_plan: Automatic: Abort rollout and revert to prior config if any of: p99 latency increase > 20% absolute or throughput decrease >15% sustained for 120s
Automatic: Gradual emergency fallback to conservative route which enforces batch_size<=8 and disables prefetch for affected endpoints
Manual: Pager alert routing to on-call infra when automatic rollback is triggered; runbook step-by-step listed in links
Postmortem: Tag experiment with incident id and create follow-up ticket for root cause
monitoring_dashboards: Console: Latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) and token-per-request histograms
Grafana: Canary cohort throughput and error budget burn rate
Alert: Canary SLO breach -> PagerDuty -> automatic rollback hook
test_plan: Unit tests for recommendation scoring and safety heuristics
Integration test that replays real traffic trace with injected heavy-tail latencies to validate rollback trigger
Chaos test: network jitter + gpu contention while canary runs to ensure fallback stability
A/B cost/quality experiment comparing baseline vs recommended profile over 72h
notes: Goal is net cost reduction with zero customer-visible SLO regressions for gold-tier customers
We must be conservative for endpoints pinned by customers (dedicated/private); controller will mark them opt-out by default
Prefer simple, interpretable anomaly signals first (EWMA deltas + count of high-latency requests) before ML blackboxes
Telemetry overhead target: <1% extra CPU and <2% extra network egress
Estimate cost savings: 8-18% on typical conversational workloads after stable rollout
